discussion_comments.comment_body: This is intentional fire-and-forget behavior, consistent with existing CLI link actions such as “Learn more.” The catch prevents an unavailable browser opener from producing an unhandled rejection, and the account dialog remains open. Adding an error state and selectable fallback URL would be a separate UX enhancement rather than part of this privacy-link change.

Fixed in bb45d79. The lookup now runs on every connected transport state (same pattern as use-agenda-tasks), so a failed or timed-out startup request recovers when the sidecar reconnects. The app URL depends only on the sidecar’s environment, not the signed-in account, so reconnect is the retry point rather than refreshAccount. Covered by a new test where the first lookup fails and the link appears after reconnecting.

The original saved draft surviving on disk narrows this finding, but does not fully dismiss it. A restored draft can be edited before sending; those edits are persisted by the sidecar send helper, not on each composer edit. If sending fails before that helper receives the edited payload, the saved record can still contain the original text/images. A failed recovery lookup then suppresses composer restoration because saved is undefined.

Reopening can recover the original copy, but that does not prove the edited payload is recoverable. This narrower case still needs an end-to-end regression through the pre-dispatch failure and reopening paths; no new live-cloud reproduction is claimed here. Any fix must distinguish definitely undispatched input from uncertain delivery rather than automatically restoring all failures.

Fixed in 469d6ee83 as a consequence of the previous fix: the catch no longer restores the captured previous mode, it sets the indicator to props.config.mode, which the runtime has rolled back to the truth. Two quick toggles that both fail therefore both resync to the same actual mode.
